lessons.title: Images and containers
lessons.summary: A container is a runtime instance created from an image.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Multiple containers can be created from the same image.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team edits a running container and expects future instances to include the fix. Rebuild and version the image with the intended change.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An image is always a running process. This is not a sound assumption; a container is a runtime instance created from an image.

lessons.takeaway: Multiple containers can be created from the same image.

lessons.title: Layering
lessons.summary: As filesystem layers plus image configuration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Later layers can hide earlier files without removing their bytes from older layers.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A secret was copied into an image and deleted in a later step. Rebuild without the secret and rotate any exposed credential.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Deleting a file in a later layer always removes it from image history. This is not a sound assumption; as filesystem layers plus image configuration.

lessons.takeaway: Later layers can hide earlier files without removing their bytes from older layers.

lessons.title: Dockerfiles
lessons.summary: Instructions for building an image.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Build inputs and base versions affect reproducibility.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A rebuild unexpectedly uses a changed base image tag. Review and pin the intended base version or digest.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is a live process supervisor for every host service. This is not a sound assumption; instructions for building an image.

lessons.takeaway: Build inputs and base versions affect reproducibility.

lessons.title: Build context
lessons.summary: The set of files made available to the build.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A dockerignore file can exclude unnecessary or sensitive inputs.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A build sends a large directory containing private files. Restrict context and add deliberate exclusion rules.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is only the Dockerfile text. This is not a sound assumption; the set of files made available to the build.

lessons.takeaway: A dockerignore file can exclude unnecessary or sensitive inputs.

lessons.title: Container logs
lessons.summary: To stdout and stderr for collection by the runtime.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Log retention and rotation still need explicit management.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Host disk fills because container logs grow without rotation. Inspect the logging driver and configure bounded retention.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Logs sent to stdout can never consume host storage. This is not a sound assumption; to stdout and stderr for collection by the runtime.

lessons.takeaway: Log retention and rotation still need explicit management.

lessons.title: Port publishing
lessons.summary: Map a host endpoint to a container port.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Exposing metadata alone does not publish a host port.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service listens inside a container but is unreachable on the host port. Check listener binding and the explicit port mapping.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: EXPOSE automatically opens every host firewall. This is not a sound assumption; map a host endpoint to a container port.

lessons.takeaway: Exposing metadata alone does not publish a host port.

lessons.title: Volumes
lessons.summary: Its lifecycle can be managed separately from the container writable layer.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Volumes still require backup and access controls.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A database loses data after its container is replaced. Move persistent data to appropriate managed storage and restore verified backups.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Deleting any container always preserves its writable-layer data. This is not a sound assumption; its lifecycle can be managed separately from the container writable layer.

lessons.takeaway: Volumes still require backup and access controls.

lessons.title: Entrypoints
lessons.summary: The service can run directly as the container's main process.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Signal forwarding differs when an intermediate shell is involved.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service ignores graceful stop because its shell wrapper mishandles signals. Use exec appropriately and verify stop behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Exec form starts an interactive shell by default. This is not a sound assumption; the service can run directly as the container's main process.

lessons.takeaway: Signal forwarding differs when an intermediate shell is involved.

lessons.title: PID one
lessons.summary: It may need to reap children and handle termination signals.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A small init can help workloads that spawn child processes.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A worker container accumulates zombie child processes. Inspect reaping behavior and use suitable process supervision.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: PID one automatically reaps every child in all applications. This is not a sound assumption; it may need to reap children and handle termination signals.

lessons.takeaway: A small init can help workloads that spawn child processes.

lessons.title: Health checks
lessons.summary: A health status based on the configured check result.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A health status alone does not guarantee automatic container restart.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A container is unhealthy but still running. Inspect health output and configure the intended supervisory response.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An unhealthy status always restarts the container in standalone Docker. This is not a sound assumption; a health status based on the configured check result.

lessons.takeaway: A health status alone does not guarantee automatic container restart.

lessons.title: User identity
lessons.summary: Reduce the privileges available to compromised application code.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Non-root execution complements other isolation controls.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An application needs write access only to one data directory. Set an appropriate user and narrow directory permissions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A non-root container has no possible security risks. This is not a sound assumption; reduce the privileges available to compromised application code.

lessons.takeaway: Non-root execution complements other isolation controls.

lessons.title: Memory limits
lessons.summary: The workload can encounter cgroup memory pressure or OOM termination.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Host free memory does not negate a container's configured limit.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A container dies while the host reports free RAM. Inspect its limit memory events and working-set demand.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A memory limit only changes monitoring display. This is not a sound assumption; the workload can encounter cgroup memory pressure or OOM termination.

lessons.takeaway: Host free memory does not negate a container's configured limit.

lessons.title: CPU quotas
lessons.summary: CPU runtime available to the cgroup over scheduling periods.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Quota throttling can affect latency.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A low-CPU-limit service has high tail latency with throttling. Compare quota demand and throttling before adjusting limits.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A CPU quota reserves an exclusive physical core automatically. This is not a sound assumption; cPU runtime available to the cgroup over scheduling periods.

lessons.takeaway: Quota throttling can affect latency.

lessons.title: Bind mounts
lessons.summary: A bind mount exposes a specified host path.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Host path permissions and contents directly affect the container.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A deployment works on one host but lacks files on another. Verify the host path and avoid hidden host-specific dependencies.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A bind mount always copies data into the image. This is not a sound assumption; a bind mount exposes a specified host path.

lessons.takeaway: Host path permissions and contents directly affect the container.

lessons.title: Read-only filesystems
lessons.summary: Reduce unintended writes to the image-derived filesystem.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Required writable paths must be provisioned separately.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A hardened container fails when writing temporary files. Provide narrowly scoped writable temporary storage.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Read-only root prevents every network attack. This is not a sound assumption; reduce unintended writes to the image-derived filesystem.

lessons.takeaway: Required writable paths must be provisioned separately.

lessons.title: Multi-stage builds
lessons.summary: Separate build tooling from the final runtime image.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Only explicitly copied artifacts need enter the final stage.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A production image contains compilers and package caches unnecessarily. Copy required runtime artifacts from a builder into a smaller final stage.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every intermediate build tool must remain in the runtime image. This is not a sound assumption; separate build tooling from the final runtime image.

lessons.takeaway: Only explicitly copied artifacts need enter the final stage.

lessons.title: Build cache
lessons.summary: It can preserve useful cached build steps.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cache keys and inputs determine whether a step can be reused.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A small source edit causes expensive dependency installation every build. Separate dependency manifests from frequently changing application source.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Docker caches every step forever regardless of inputs. This is not a sound assumption; it can preserve useful cached build steps.

lessons.takeaway: Cache keys and inputs determine whether a step can be reused.

lessons.title: Secrets in builds
lessons.summary: Use a dedicated build secret mechanism.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Secrets should not be baked into layers or ordinary build arguments.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A dependency download requires a private registry credential. Use scoped build secrets and verify the final image contains no credential.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Build arguments are always encrypted and excluded from history. This is not a sound assumption; use a dedicated build secret mechanism.

lessons.takeaway: Secrets should not be baked into layers or ordinary build arguments.

lessons.title: Image digests
lessons.summary: Specific content-addressed image data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Mutable tags can move to different content.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two deployments of the same tag run different builds. Record and deploy the intended immutable digest.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A digest is just a friendly mutable alias. This is not a sound assumption; specific content-addressed image data.

lessons.takeaway: Mutable tags can move to different content.

lessons.title: Networks
lessons.summary: Scoped container connectivity with built-in name resolution.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Network attachment and published host ports are distinct choices.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two containers expected to communicate are attached to different networks. Inspect network membership and intended service names.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every container name resolves globally across unrelated networks. This is not a sound assumption; scoped container connectivity with built-in name resolution.

lessons.takeaway: Network attachment and published host ports are distinct choices.

lessons.title: Compose dependencies
lessons.summary: A started dependency may not yet be ready to serve requests.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Readiness checks and application retry behavior remain important.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An application starts before its database becomes usable. Use readiness-aware orchestration and bounded connection retries.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Starting a database process proves schema initialization is complete. This is not a sound assumption; a started dependency may not yet be ready to serve requests.

lessons.takeaway: Readiness checks and application retry behavior remain important.

lessons.title: Restart policy
lessons.summary: Runtime behavior when a container exits under specified conditions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Restarting repeatedly does not repair an underlying bad configuration.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A container exits immediately because a required setting is missing. Inspect exit logs and correct configuration before relying on restarts.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A restart policy fixes every application bug. This is not a sound assumption; runtime behavior when a container exits under specified conditions.

lessons.takeaway: Restarting repeatedly does not repair an underlying bad configuration.

lessons.title: Registry access
lessons.summary: They grant different capabilities at different lifecycle stages.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Credentials should have the minimum required repository scope.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A runtime workload can overwrite the image it was deployed from. Reduce registry credential scope and separate build from runtime identities.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A registry password is always safe to embed in an image. This is not a sound assumption; they grant different capabilities at different lifecycle stages.

lessons.takeaway: Credentials should have the minimum required repository scope.

lessons.title: Resource cleanup
lessons.summary: Unused from the runtime's perspective may still be operationally valuable.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Volume deletion can remove persistent data.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host is low on disk and an operator proposes deleting every volume. Identify consumers and backups before scoped cleanup.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every prune operation is harmless to recoverability. This is not a sound assumption; unused from the runtime's perspective may still be operationally valuable.

lessons.takeaway: Volume deletion can remove persistent data.

lessons.title: Socket exposure
lessons.summary: Daemon access can grant extensive control over the host.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Treat daemon API access as a privileged trust boundary.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A web application mounts the daemon socket for convenience. Remove unnecessary daemon access or isolate a narrowly controlled service.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The socket grants only read-only log access by default. This is not a sound assumption; daemon access can grant extensive control over the host.

lessons.takeaway: Treat daemon API access as a privileged trust boundary.

lessons.title: Rootless mode
lessons.summary: The need for a root-privileged daemon and containers.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rootless operation has compatibility and resource-control considerations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team wants to reduce daemon privilege on developer hosts. Evaluate rootless support against networking storage and workload requirements.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Rootless mode removes all kernel attack surface. This is not a sound assumption; the need for a root-privileged daemon and containers.

lessons.takeaway: Rootless operation has compatibility and resource-control considerations.

lessons.title: Image scanning
lessons.summary: Evidence about known issues in the inspected image and metadata.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A clean scan is not proof of absence of all vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A scan finds a critical library issue in a deployed image. Assess reachability and impact then rebuild and redeploy a verified fix.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Scanning guarantees application logic is secure. This is not a sound assumption; evidence about known issues in the inspected image and metadata.

lessons.takeaway: A clean scan is not proof of absence of all vulnerabilities.

lessons.title: Supply chain
lessons.summary: Establish evidence about artifact origin and integrity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Verification policy must define trusted identities and sources.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A registry contains an unexpected image under a trusted-looking tag. Verify digest provenance and the authorized publishing identity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any signed image is automatically safe regardless of signer. This is not a sound assumption; establish evidence about artifact origin and integrity.

lessons.takeaway: Verification policy must define trusted identities and sources.

lessons.title: Shared kernel
lessons.summary: Kernel vulnerabilities can cross container isolation boundaries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Host patching remains important even with minimal images.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host kernel vulnerability affects container isolation. Assess host exposure and roll out host remediation safely.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Each container always has an independent kernel. This is not a sound assumption; kernel vulnerabilities can cross container isolation boundaries.

lessons.takeaway: Host patching remains important even with minimal images.

lessons.title: Stateful migration
lessons.summary: Persistent data or schema changes may outlive the old image.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Application and data compatibility must be considered together.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A new image migrates the database schema incompatibly. Plan compatible migration or verified data recovery before rollback.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Restoring an old image automatically reverses all schema changes. This is not a sound assumption; persistent data or schema changes may outlive the old image.

lessons.takeaway: Application and data compatibility must be considered together.
